terra.problem: The LORD tells Joshua and all the people to arise; the text does not say Joshua must get up first.
The promise was made to Moses, but the text does not say it was made before Joshua ever heard it.
This explanation is almost identical to the one for True. Explanations should sound different from one another.
Joshua's service as Moses' assistant does not establish that he saw what the LORD being with Moses looked like. Saying it is now his turn also suggests the LORD had not been with him before.
The explanation is flat and repetitive: after the quotation, both remaining sentences simply restate that the job concerns the land.
The straight-road comparison repeats the comparison used in the explanation for True.
The command says day and night; it does not specify every hour between.
Joshua says the crossing will be within three days, not necessarily three days away.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the answer and quotation, without Papa Dorin's natural voice.
Joshua says the wives, young children and livestock may remain; the explanation states that the families stay. It also says the men go, rather than specifying the mighty men of valor.
Joshua permits the wives, young children and livestock to remain; the explanation states that the families stay put.
The text says the wives, young children and livestock may stay, not that the families do stay.
